content.user_title: Build and Test Reliable AI Skills
content.value_statement: AI skills often fail because triggers, instructions, and tests are unclear. This skill provides a structured method for writing, testing, and refining them.
actual_capabilities: Defines a recommended SKILL.md structure with concise frontmatter and searchable trigger descriptions.
Maps test-driven development phases to skill creation and revision.
Provides pressure-scenario methods for testing agent compliance and identifying unclear instructions.
Explains skill naming, cross-references, token efficiency, examples, and file organization.
Includes a Graphviz utility that renders dot blocks from SKILL.md files into SVG diagrams.
Supplies checklists for authoring, testing, refinement, and deployment.
limitations: The guidance focuses on instruction-based skills and may not cover every marketplace format.
Pressure tests require access to subagents or repeated model sessions.
The graph renderer requires Node.js and a local Graphviz installation.
The included persuasion guidance needs careful review to preserve user control and instruction priority.

use_cases.title: Create a New Skill
use_cases.description: Draft a focused skill with clear triggers, concise instructions, useful examples, and a deployment checklist.

use_cases.title: Improve Existing Instructions
use_cases.description: Review a skill for discovery problems, unnecessary detail, weak examples, and unclear requirements.

use_cases.title: Test Agent Compliance
use_cases.description: Design baseline and pressure scenarios, record failures, revise instructions, and verify improved behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a skill for [task]. Define a clear name, trigger-only description, overview, steps, and common mistakes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Starting a new skill from a known workflow

prompt_templates.title: Review Skill Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SKILL.md for discovery, clarity, token efficiency, structure, and realistic examples. Return prioritized edits with reasons.
prompt_templates.scenario: Improving an existing skill before testing

prompt_templates.title: Design Pressure Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Design three pressure scenarios for this discipline skill. Include baseline behavior, expected compliance, failure signals, and a retest plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluating whether instructions remain effective under pressure

prompt_templates.title: Run an Iterative Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a RED-GREEN-REFACTOR audit of [skill]. Identify rationalizations, revise the smallest necessary sections, and define verification criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Refining an advanced skill through repeated agent tests

output_examples.input: Create a skill for diagnosing intermittent test failures.
output_examples.output: A concise skill draft with trigger-focused metadata, a diagnostic workflow, one representative example, common mistakes, and a verification checklist.

output_examples.input: Review this long skill for discovery and token efficiency.
output: Rewrite the description to contain triggers only.
Move detailed references into supporting files.
Keep one complete example and remove repeated explanations.

output_examples.input: Test whether this deployment skill resists deadline pressure.
output_examples.output: Three realistic scenarios, baseline expectations, compliance criteria, likely rationalizations, and a focused revision plan.

best_practices: Run a baseline scenario before writing or revising instructions.
Keep descriptions focused on activation conditions, not the full workflow.
Retest after each focused change and record exact failure reasoning.
anti_patterns: Do not create skills for one-time project details.
Do not repeat large workflows when a clear cross-reference is sufficient.
Do not use coercive language that conflicts with user control or higher-priority instructions.

faq.question: What types of skills does this guidance support?
faq.answer: It supports technique, pattern, reference, and discipline-focused skills, with different testing methods for each type.

faq.question: Does it create skills automatically?
faq.answer: It provides authoring and testing guidance. The agent still drafts files, runs evaluations, and applies revisions.

faq.question: Why test a documentation skill?
faq.answer: Testing reveals unclear triggers, missing steps, and rationalizations that a document review may not expose.

faq.question: Is Graphviz required?
faq.answer: Graphviz is required only for the optional diagram renderer. The writing and testing guidance works without it.

faq.question: Can it review an existing SKILL.md?
faq.answer: Yes. It can assess discovery, structure, examples, token efficiency, testing coverage, and deployment readiness.

faq.question: Does it guarantee consistent agent behavior?
faq.answer: No. Model behavior varies, so repeated tests and clear safety boundaries remain necessary.
